turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Hey, quick vitals before he comes in. Blood pressure is one twenty-eight over eighty-four, pulse ninety-two, oxygen ninety-eight percent, and you weighed in at one seventy-one pounds.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-eight, is that bad? Sorry, I spiral about numbers.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Ninety-eight percent is fine, really. Any drug allergies?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no allergies. Um, is he running behind? I've been worrying since I got here.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Just a few minutes. Med list has ferrous sulfate, three hundred twenty-five milligrams, once a day.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): That dose isn't what I take. They're the green tablets, sixty-five milligrams, and I only take them sometimes, when I remember.
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm her sister, I stay over to help out. She skips that iron all the time. She's been exhausted for eight months, easy.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It has not been eight months. The real exhaustion started about three months ago.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): I'll let the doctor untangle the dose. He's on his way.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the computer just ate my login again. I'm Dr. Ellison. What brings you in?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm tired all the time, I get breathless, and my periods have been heavy for about a year. Be straight with me, could this be cancer?
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Cancer's not where I'm starting. Say the period part again? I clicked into the wrong chart.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Heavy for about a year. On the bad days I go through a ton of pads, I don't sit and count them, and there are clots, some little, some bigger. I don't measure those either.
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She bleeds through constantly, day and night. She can barely finish a shift at the store.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I still finish my shifts at the grocery store. It's the heavy days, not every single day. And I'm not breathless just sitting here. It's when I walk.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): When you walk, okay. How long has the shortness of breath been going on?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks... well, actually, closer to three months. Yeah, three months. I have to stop once on the stairs.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She gets short of breath just sitting on the couch. I've watched it happen.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not true. Sitting is fine. It's only when I move, please don't put the other thing down.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain when you're walking?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. I haven't fainted. I just feel worn out, and sometimes my heart pounds on the stairs. Do I need a transfusion? I was up half the night reading about that.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): I can't say transfusion until we see a blood count. Hang on, the tiredness, how long did you say? The screen refreshed and I lost my place.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Eight months.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): About three. I know which one it is.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between three and eight months, and we'll leave it unconfirmed. Did someone say hair?
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Clumps in the shower drain. Her mother was on thyroid pills for years, hypothyroidism.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): The hair loss is real, but I cannot date it. Last winter, or the one before, sometime after the holidays, I really don't know. And yes, Mom had hypothyroidism. Does that mean mine is failing too?
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): I don't know that yet. Any fever lately?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. So what tests? How many needles? I get queasy just thinking about it.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Exam first, if this thing lets me type. Go ahead and take a deep breath for me.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear, heart sounds regular, I don't hear a murmur. The inside of your lower eyelids looks pale. No swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Pale, so that's anemia, right? Should I be taking more iron? I always forget the real name, they're just those green ones.

[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Green ones are ferrous sulfate. I want you on ferrous sulfate three hundred... no, three hundred twenty-five milligrams by mouth once a day, every day, not just when you remember. Stop the sixty-five milligram tablets.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day? What if it tears up my stomach? What if I throw it up? Is three twenty-five even safe?
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take it with a little food if your stomach complains. If you vomit a dose, skip it, don't double up the next day. Three twenty-five is a usual treatment dose.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. My friend had a pelvic scan and they found fibroids. Do I need that? Does it hurt? I really hate procedures.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the labs come back very low, or the bleeding isn't settling, we might get a pelvic ultrasound. I'm not booking it today. It doesn't hurt.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): And the bloodwork, is that today? I hate needles. I just want to know how many tubes.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): A CBC, a ferritin, and a TSH today. I almost tacked on a chemistry panel... actually no, skip the chemistry, just those three.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): TSH is the thyroid test, right? So you do think I have what my mom had?

[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): My working impression is this may be iron deficiency from the heavy bleeding. I can't rule out a thyroid issue, given your mom and the fatigue, but I'm not calling that today.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She also freezes. Sweater on in the house, and it's been warm out.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not freeze. I'm tired, not cold. That sweater is for the grocery store, their air conditioning is ridiculous.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any bleeding from the gums or the nose?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Can I keep working? And if I get worse before I see you, will somebody actually call me?

[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep working if you feel up to it. If you soak through a pad every hour, or you feel faint, go to the ER. If a result is urgent we'll call you sooner. Otherwise I'll see you back in two weeks.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks sounds long. What if the iron constipates me, do I stop it?
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Don't stop it for mild constipation. Drink more water, and we'll talk about it at that two-week visit. I have to finish this note before the next one.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
